title: Improving art and animation
author: Enjoyooooor
selftext: Hey guys I am really trying to polish my animation and art style. Would love some feedback on how it currently looks and what I could do to improve/polish my workflow.

comments.author: deezwhatbro
comments.body: Gameplay shows promise but looks a bit generic. You haven’t shared your workflow so I can’t really say much there.

replies.author: Enjoyooooor
replies.body: Hey there, work flow is generating base images through grok/chatgpt then animating through autosprite.

replies.author: deezwhatbro
replies.body: Gotcha. Thanks! I guess I would recommend some more Idle animations like breathing. Ambient particles (the bird was a nice touch) Humanoid character art doesn’t seem to blend with the animals so maybe try to add some more theme guardrails via text prompts and/or environment sheets. The pixel art text seems a bit out of place as well. It reminds me of MapleStory a little bit which is very nostalgic but also adds a bit to the “generic” feeling. Still though, I think it’s a great direction so far.

comments.author: Enjoyooooor
comments.body: Thank you for taking the time it’s much appreciated. I was really happy with the birds too haha. And my combat text is based off maplestory so you have a great eye. I will be looking into generating more idle animations and ambient particles.

comments.author: IsThisASnakeInMyBoot
comments.body:
I'm a little confused about when you say "polish my art style" because almost every character is literally drawn in completely different art styles. The guy on the left is like cartoony/chibi, the main character is sort of generic anime style, the dog and the cat are cutesy, the merchant is like idk studio ghibli-ish, then the gearsmith is a whole different style again. There's no real cohesion so it's very jarring.

The game itself seems simple but honestly not even bad at all, I just don't know what \*your\* art style is. Is any of the art yours, or is it all generated? I'm not saying that as a diss or anything, I'm just trying to highlight that there's a huge disconnect there. Having a core aesthetic that goes beyond "anime style" would help, anime itself has tons of different art styles which is part of the issue when you ask AI to generate "anime style" images. It just goes for this boring generic middle ground. I think what might help is settling on a specific style that you want to achieve and then trying to get the characters, the backgrounds and everything to line up with that.

replies.author: Enjoyooooor
replies.body: Hey thanks for taking the time ,  I can see what you’re saying with the art style and is something I’ve been trying to improve. Only the left most character is my art everything else is generated. Going to look into tightening my gen prompts.

comments.author: ModernGameDev
comments.body:
I honestly think the animation has too many frames. Seeing the motion looks unnatural especially for a pixel art game. Try removing some of the in between frames and start more simple.

This video is 4 years old but still applies today & it helped me learn more about animation: https://youtu.be/pF--YKCCUMw?is=ylT9x8cPViyQE\_Id

replies.author: Enjoyooooor
replies.body: Thanks for this, watching it now. I actually originally was using 6-8 frames in beginning but got frustrated with how they were turning out so I just ended up using all 16 frames (autosprite minimum is 16frame)
